questions.stem: The Gond, the largest tribal community of India, are found mainly in:
questions.explanation: The Gonds — numbering over 13 million — are concentrated in Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha. Famous Gond kingdoms ruled Gondwana (central India) in the medieval period. Rani Durgavati (d. 1564) was a Gond queen who fought Akbar's forces. Gond paintings (pitora / digna) have a distinctive dotted style.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Match the tribal community with the state/region where they are principally found. A. Toda. B. Bhil. C. Khasi. D. Santhal. List-II: 1. Nilgiris (Tamil Nadu), 2. Gujarat/Rajasthan/MP, 3. Meghalaya, 4. Jharkhand / West Bengal.
questions.explanation: Toda — pastoralists of the Nilgiri hills (Tamil Nadu), famous for buffalo herding and barrel-vaulted 'munds'. Bhil — spread across MP, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra — second-largest tribal group in India. Khasi — Meghalaya (with Garo and Jaintia); matrilineal society. Santhal — largest tribal group in Jharkhand, West Bengal and Odisha; Santhal rebellion of 1855-56 was a major anti-British uprising.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Jarawa, Onge and Sentinelese — 'Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups' (PVTGs) — live in:
questions.explanation: The Andaman Islands are home to several PVTGs of Negrito origin — Jarawa, Onge, Great Andamanese, and the uncontacted Sentinelese of North Sentinel Island. The Nicobar group has the Nicobarese and the Shompen. Their numbers are tiny (the Sentinelese are thought to be fewer than 100) and all are legally protected from outside contact. Lakshadweep has the mainly Muslim Minicoy / Amini communities.

questions.stem: The Bodo tribe, with its own constitutionally-recognised language, is concentrated in:
questions.explanation: Bodos are the largest plains tribe of Assam; concentrated in the Bodoland Territorial Region on the north bank of the Brahmaputra. Bodo was added to the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Amendment (2003), along with Dogri, Maithili and Santhali. The 2020 Bodo Peace Accord created the Bodoland Territorial Council with wider autonomy.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Apatani' tribe — famous for its permanent wet-rice terraces without the use of draft animals — lives in:
questions.explanation: The Apatani live in the Ziro valley of Lower Subansiri district, Arunachal Pradesh. Their landscape is on UNESCO's tentative World Heritage list for its terraced wet-rice cultivation integrated with fish farming in the paddies — without the use of draft animals or chemical fertilisers. The women were famously tattooed with nose plugs (a practice now discontinued).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: 'Birsa Munda' — a tribal hero celebrated on 'Janjatiya Gaurav Divas' (15 November) — belonged to which community?
questions.explanation: Birsa Munda (1875-1900) led the 'Ulgulan' tribal uprising in the Chotanagpur region against British colonial rule and Christian missionaries. Died in prison aged 25. 15 November — his birth anniversary — has been observed as 'Janjatiya Gaurav Divas' since 2021. The Gonds, Santhals and Bhils had their own rebellion leaders — Tantia Bhil, Sido and Kanhu Murmu (Santhals).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The constitutional provisions for Scheduled Tribes — special reservations in education, jobs and legislatures — are found mainly in:

options.option_text: Part XVI (Special provisions for SC / ST)

questions.explanation: Part XVI (Articles 330-342) contains special provisions — reservation of seats in Lok Sabha (Art 330) and state Legislative Assemblies (Art 332), reservation in services (Art 335), the National Commissions for SC and ST (Art 338 / 338A), the Fifth Schedule (tribal areas in most states) and the Sixth Schedule (tribal areas in the NE). These reservations were initially meant for 10 years but have been extended periodically.
